core_message: Precision engineering and desperate courage breached Germany's vital dams, but at an immense human cost on both sides.
title: How did bouncing bombs break German dams?
description:
On the night of May 16, 1943, nineteen specially modified Lancaster bombers took off on one of the most audacious air raids of World War II. Flying at tree-top height into heavily defended airspace, 617 Squadron aimed to breach Germany's critical industrial dams using experimental bouncing bombs.

Invented by engineer Barnes Wallis, the Upkeep weapon required extreme precision: flying at exactly sixty feet altitude and 240 miles per hour under intense flak. This is the complete story of the Dambusters Raid, its technical triumphs, and its devastating aftermath.

Based on the Wikipedia article "Operation Chastise" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Chastise), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.
